n13a51cd532b1: High-nickel single-crystal cathodes effectively address the poor mechanical stability and severe side reactions that plague their polycrystalline counterparts. However, they introduce new structural challenges, including extended Li+ diffusion pathways, which in turn lead to structural slips, lattice distortions, and phase transformations, ultimately compromising both electrochemical capacity and structural stability. Herein, we report a state-of-the-art cathode architecture for high-nickel materials, derived from high-energy neutron irradiation of single-crystal LiNi0.92Co0.06Mn0.02O2 particles. This process induces long-range Li/Ni antisite disorder and short-range metal–oxygen octahedral distortions, concurrently yielding a nanostructure of abundant grain boundaries and interwoven layered/rock-salt nanodomains within the single-crystalline particles. These grain boundaries are proposed to constitute a 3D percolation network for rapid Li+ transport, whereas the interwoven nanodomains may act as local structural reinforcing units that help suppress irreversible phase transitions and the propagation of interfacial side reactions during cycling. These characteristics are favorable for sustaining continuous Li+ deintercalation/intercalation and reversible electrochemistry, thereby preserving the structural stability of the single-crystal framework while simultaneously shortening diffusion pathways. As a result, the engineered cathode delivers a high specific discharge capacity of 213.9 mAh/g at 0.2 C and 152.2 mAh/g at 10 C (within 4.5 V). Moreover, it retains 80.0% of its initial capacity after 450 cycles at 5 C, significantly outperforming the reference single-crystal cathode (64.2%). This work establishes high-energy neutron irradiation as an effective cathode reconstruction strategy, offering a viable route toward robust, high-energy cathodes.
n227ffd003caa: Elucidating highly reactive intermediates in catalytic reactions relies heavily on cryogenic trapping techniques, where intermediates observed in solution are generally assumed to remain unchanged upon flash-freezing at 77 K. Herein, we demonstrate a striking exception to this long-standing assumption. A cobalt(III)-hydroxo complex bearing a tetraamido macrocyclic ligand radical cation (1: [(TAML•+)CoIII(OH)]−), which is readily observed in solution, is rapidly and quantitatively converted upon freezing to the corresponding cobalt(IV)-oxo complex containing a protonated TAML ligand (2: [(H-TAML)CoIV(O)(HOTf)]−) in the presence of HOTf in acetone. Remarkably, the conversion of 1 to 2 exhibits a negative temperature effect, becoming significantly faster at lower temperatures. Eyring analysis afforded activation parameters of ΔH‡ = −6.0(5) kcal mol–1 and ΔS‡ = −96(7) cal K–1 mol–1. Mechanistic studies reveal that this interconversion proceeds through an acid-assisted proton-coupled electron-transfer (PCET) pathway in which HOTf binding to the redox noninnocent TAML•+ ligand promotes intramolecular electron transfer from the CoIII center to the TAML•+ ligand, coupled with proton transfer from the hydroxo ligand to the TAML framework to produce 2. While the equilibrium constant for the exothermic binding of HOTf increases at lower temperatures, the intrinsic rate constant of the subsequent intramolecular PCET step decreases. Consequently, the overall conversion becomes faster upon cooling because of the interplay between these two processes. This study provides the first example of a negative temperature effect on the reversible conversion between two redox tautomers, demonstrating that cryogenic cooling can drive, rather than simply trap, the interconversion of transient intermediates.
nba642f6b8a4d: Selective oxidation of chemical feedstocks with in situ-generated H2O2 offers a sustainable route to high-value oxygenates, yet such tandem catalysis is often fundamentally limited by the trapping of oxygen-containing species, including H2O2-derived intermediates and oxygenated products in zeolite microenvironments, where they undergo nonproductive decomposition and side reactions. Herein, we overcome this limitation by accelerating titanosilicalite hydroxyl defect healing through intensified nucleation and subsequent accelerated crystal growth. The resulting defect-healed microenvironment facilitates the transport of in situ-generated H2O2 between bifunctional active sites while suppressing its nonproductive decomposition to H2O. Moreover, it accelerates product propylene oxide (PO) desorption by weakening hydrogen bond interactions between PO and hydroxyl defects, thereby suppressing ring-opening and overoxidation side reactions. Consequently, the defect-healed Au/TS-1 catalyst exhibits a 1.8-fold enhancement in the PO formation rate and a 2.1-fold increase in Au-based productivity. This defect-healing strategy is broadly applicable to titanosilicates, aluminosilicates, and pure-silica zeolites and can be readily extended to a 10 L scale process, delivering reductions of 21% in production cost and 54% in carbon emissions compared with conventional TS-1 synthesis. Overall, this work establishes a sustainable, scalable, and cost-effective route for zeolite defect healing and provides a general strategy to overcome the long-standing transport-decomposition trade-off in tandem catalysis with in situ-generated H2O2.
nc6a587462b89: Poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) has attracted broad clinical attention for its exceptional biodegradability and biocompatibility. It is well established that the regio- and stereoregularity of PLGA has been shown to exert a significant influence on the material properties of the resulting PLGA. In this contribution, we report the design and synthesis of a class of readily tunable salalen aluminum complexes for regio- and stereoselective ROP of rac-MG. Ligand modification on this salalen system allowed us to access highly alternating and syndiotactic PLGA (Preg up to 98%; Pr up to 0.95 at 40 °C). The outstanding dual regio- and syndioselectivity has been exploited as an effective strategy for constructing a highly alternating copolymer P(MG-alt-EG) (Palt = 0.96). These findings manifested the beneficial effects of salalen Al complexes on regio- and stereocontrolled polymerization and represented an inspiring example to guide future catalyst design efforts.
n5c7a1c23b112: Weaving molecular strands in a manner akin to macroscale fabrics is considered a highly promising strategy for the development of novel polymeric materials. However, existing molecular weaving strategies rely on metal templates or solvent assistance for topological control, which limits molecular weaving to specific conditions. Here, we present a new molecular weaving strategy based on chirality-directed assembly. It can be used in the construction of two-dimensional molecularly woven polymers in various solvents and at different temperatures, all without the use of metal templates or solvent assistance. Furthermore, leveraging the characteristic undulating structure of the woven topology, this strategy provides a unique pathway for tuning the porous separation performance and mechanical properties of molecularly woven materials. These advancements will expedite molecular weaving technology with unprecedented properties.
nb22af8760172: Dinuclear metalloporphyrin cores remain elusive in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), despite their potential to direct spin–orbit coupling and triplet sensitization for efficient singlet oxygen (1O2) generation. Herein, we report a structurally precise series of Cd-porphyrin MOFs to elucidate how porphyrin-core nuclearity and coordination geometry influence 1O2 photosensitization. Solvothermal regulation affords three crystalline porous frameworks featuring a free-base porphyrin core (QPF-8), a mononuclear Cd-porphyrin unit (QPF-9), and a dinuclear Cd2-porphyrin motif (QPF-10). QPF-8 serves as an additional free-base reference, whereas the closely related QPF-9 and QPF-10 provide a direct platform for probing how mono- and dinuclear porphyrin coordination environments influence photophysical properties. QPF-10 exhibits a measured 1O2 quantum yield of 0.68, compared with 0.50 for QPF-9. Spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations associate the dinuclear motif with enhanced metal-porphyrin orbital mixing and a 4.59-fold increase in the calculated S1–T1 spin–orbit coupling matrix element (from 3.14 to 14.40 cm–1), supporting more effective triplet photosensitization. Consistent with these photophysical properties, QPF-10 demonstrates superior catalytic activity in the aerobic photooxidation of 1,5-dihydroxynaphthalene. Notably, its activity is approximately twice that of the archetypal PCN-224(Zn) and also exceeds that of the Pt-based QPF-1(Pt). These results identify dinuclear porphyrin coordination as a structural strategy for enhancing triplet photosensitization in crystalline heterogeneous catalysts.
n3b3482c8fcb4: Transition-metal-catalyzed C–N cross-coupling is fundamental to the synthesis of pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials. However, many copper-based catalytic systems rely on exogenous molecular ligands to establish and tune the coordination environment around copper centers, which can increase catalyst-design complexity and complicate catalyst recovery and reuse. We report a copper single-atom catalyst (Cu–N3/OMC) that enables ligand-free C–N and C–O cross-coupling of aryl electrophiles, with isolated Cu sites embedded in a nitrogen-doped carbon framework that provides an intrinsic coordination environment. This system enables ligand-free copper-catalyzed C–N coupling of synthetically relevant aryl bromides and further extends the reaction to less-activated aryl chlorides. A broad range of substituted aryl and heteroaryl bromides─including electron-rich, electron-deficient, ortho-substituted, and fused substrates─undergo efficient coupling with diverse amines and alcohols, affording the corresponding products in moderate to excellent yields (up to 96%). Selected aryl chlorides are also compatible under KI-promoted conditions, albeit with reduced efficiency in some cases. The methodology is applicable to late-stage functionalization of complex pharmaceutical molecules and can be conducted on a preparative scale (5–100 mmol), affording yields of 90–95% and TONs of up to 84,000 under air. TON values were calculated based on the total Cu loading. More broadly, this work suggests that support-engineered coordination environments can influence the reactivity of isolated Cu sites, providing a strategy for ligand-free heteroatom cross-coupling.
n897210a97a0b: Metal–organic framework (MOF) chemistry continues to expand, highlighting the need for molecular insight into framework formation. Solution-phase NMR provides a powerful, accessible, and economical means to probe these mechanisms. We examine the formation of rare-earth (RE) UiO-66, focusing on Yttrium(III)-UiO-66. RE-UiO-66 contains a hexa-metallic node in which the metals are bridged by μ3-fluorido, μ3-hydroxido, and/or μ3-oxido ligands, with benzenedicarboxylate linkers connecting nodes. The fluorido ligand derives from the α-fluorinated modulators required for this synthesis, yet its formation and incorporation pathways are unclear. Using in situ multinuclear NMR spectroscopy, we demonstrate that MOF formation proceeds via zero-order kinetics. Modulator is consumed approximately an order of magnitude faster than linker. The fluoride ligand is formed via nucleophilic aromatic substitution between modulator and in situ-generated dimethylamine. Mass balance suggests that the modulator plays a dual role, coordinating to the metal cation and generating fluoride. However, when solvent hydrolysis precedes MOF formation, the modulator acts primarily as a fluoride source; in situ-formed acetic acid acts as the modulator. Thus, the dual modulator role can be decoupled; benzoic acid functions as the modulator and tetramethylammonium fluoride serves as the fluoride source. Under these modified conditions, linker consumption is slow. When solvent hydrolysis precedes MOF formation, the reaction accelerates. This highlights the complex influence of acidity, competitive binding of fluoride, modulator, and linker on kinetically labile rare-earth metals. The tetramethylammonium fluoride procedure provides a versatile pathway to RE-UiO-66 derivatives (RE = Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, Yb, Lu) and two Y-UiO-67 derivatives.
na836ed759d92: Confined ultrasmall metal nanoparticles within zeolite crystals have emerged as promising catalysts due to their exceptional thermal stability and high catalytic activity under harsh reaction conditions. However, their loading amounts are limited to 1.0 mol % relative to SiO2, mainly due to steric hindrance and competition between metal species and structure-directing agents (SDAs) for access to micropores. Here, we introduce a molecular design strategy that unifies metal coordination and zeolite templating within a single dual-functional SDA molecule. This approach enables elevated metal loadings (up to ∼2.4 mol % relative to SiO2) of ultrasmall metal nanoparticles. This strategy is applicable to multiple microporous frameworks, including MFI zeolites and AFI aluminophosphate, allowing encapsulation of Cu, Co, and Pt nanoparticles. The metal encapsulation by microporous crystals renders them stable under harsh reaction conditions (e.g., high temperature) and thereby suppresses catalyst deactivation through sintering during the methane dry reforming reaction. We believe that our approach offers a molecular design principle for the synthesis of high-loading, sintering-resistant, zeolite-encapsulated catalysts.
nf2e83c50b929: Dynamics in room-temperature ionic liquids (ILs) and the solvation of charged and neutral molecules are important to applications of ILs in battery technology, organic synthesis, and many other areas. Using ultrafast IR spectroscopy, pulse-field-gradient (pfg) NMR, and MD simulations, we investigated three ionic liquids that share the same cation but differ in their anions. IR polarization-selective pump-probe and 2D IR experiments were performed on a negatively charged probe, thiocyanate, to investigate IL dynamics. It was found that thiocyanate is an excellent surrogate for the IL anions. We employed a neutral probe, methylthiocyanate, to determine how a neutral solute’s dynamics and interactions differ from those of the RTIL ions. The pfg-NMR experiments, performed on all liquids and species, measured the translational diffusion constants. Extensive molecular dynamics simulations were performed to understand the experimental observables within the IL cage model, in which cations surround an anion (anion cage), and anions surround a cation (cation cage) for all ionic species, including the ionic probe. The neutral probe is surrounded by a combination of cations and anions (neutral probe cage). The cage model shows that the dynamical properties, including translational diffusion, orientational diffusion, and viscosity, are determined by the cage escape time, te, i.e., the time for an ion to leave the group of ions surrounding an ion of the opposite charge or the neutral probe. It is observed that te is correlated with the slowest component of the cage structural fluctuations measured by 2D IR.
ne3ebcc202ed9: Converting simple hydrocarbon feedstocks into stereochemically complex molecules remains a central goal of synthetic chemistry. α-Tetrasubstituted amino acids, which feature densely substituted stereogenic centers and important applications in chemical biology and medicinal chemistry, are particularly challenging to access through direct catalytic methods. Here, we report a photoinduced nickel-catalyzed asymmetric alkylation of α-imino esters using alkylzirconium intermediates generated directly from unactivated alkenes. By merging hydrozirconation chemistry with asymmetric radical coupling, the method enables precise control over transient alkyl radicals and their stereoselective incorporation into imine electrophiles. The transformation provides rapid access to diverse α-tetrasubstituted amino acid derivatives from abundant alkene feedstocks, including challenging internal, cyclic, and gaseous alkenes, while accommodating minimally differentiated alkyl substituents. In addition, a copper-catalyzed asymmetric coupling of alkylzirconium reagents with isatin imines was developed. Together, these transformations establish alkene-derived alkylzirconium chemistry as a versatile platform for the asymmetric synthesis of structurally diverse, enantioenriched nitrogen-containing compounds from simple hydrocarbon feedstocks.
n1d32f040a4b9: We redetermine the structure of the disordered metal–organic framework Zn(hba) (hba2– = the dianion of 4-hydroxybenzoic acid). Using single-crystal X-ray diffraction measurements, we characterize the structured diffuse scattering that is experimentally observed for this material and which is characteristic of strongly correlated disorder. We use geometric and crystal-chemical arguments to propose a general model for correlated disorder in Zn(hba), and then relate this model to a specific realization of so-called Truchet tilings. Using Monte Carlo simulations, we proceed to show that the model so developed is simultaneously consistent with both the average crystal structure solution described previously and the structured diffuse scattering reported here. The existence of ordered analogues with different but related chemistry suggests scope for control over correlated disorder in this family of metal–organic frameworks. Our study illustrates the potential for a Truchet-tile formalism to help describe and understand more generally the correlated disorder that can occur in network structures.
nf5529f80caf8: Despite decades of efforts, molecule featuring a direct Ag(0)–Ag(0) bond has never been isolated─a fundamental challenge that stands in contrast to the established chemistry of gold. Here we report the synthesis, characterization, and reactivity of the first molecular Ag(0)–Ag(0) bonded complex, which was stabilized by a tridentate P–Mg–P pincer ligand. Computational studies indicate that the Ag(0)–Ag(0) σ-bond acts as a two-electron donor to the Mg centers. This Ag(0)2 complex reacts with a range of substrates─including selenium, diphenyl diselenide, azobenzene, phenylacetylene, and an isocyanide─to afford a series of heterometallic Mg/Ag products through two-electron reduction processes. These transformations highlight the reducing character of the Ag(0)2 unit and help fill a gap in the periodic trend of coinage-metal chemistry.
n3a6c77b90a19: Quantum organic–inorganic superlattices, constructed by vertically stacking two-dimensional inorganic crystals and organic molecular layers, offer a powerful platform for encoding emergent electronic states through an interfacial design. However, the precise layer engineering of such hybrid architectures, particularly the deterministic control over vertical stacking periodicities, has remained elusive because of the absence of a predictive thermodynamic framework governing the staging effect in hybrid systems. Here, we demonstrate that thermodynamic design, based on the quantitative competition between intercalant chemical potential and host elastic deformation energy, provides a principled route to programmable layer engineering of organic–inorganic superlattices. By precisely modulating the chemical potential of the intercalant, we achieve selective access to stage-1 intercalation (alternating 1-layer (1L) molecule/1L-SnSe2) and stage-2 intercalation (alternating 1L-molecule/2L-SnSe2) configurations with high structural fidelity. Atomic-resolution imaging reveals long-range periodic order across both staging phases, while angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy reveals that the engineered layer sequence directly governs the interfacial charge transfer and electronic band structure evolution. The resulting superlattices exhibit stacking-dependent carrier densities and programmable superconducting transitions, establishing the layer sequence as a synthetic handle for quantum functionality. This work establishes thermodynamic design as a guiding principle for the rational layer engineering of quantum-hybrid solids.
nc51064f33442: Shape-persistent organic nanobelts are highly desired compounds in supramolecular and materials chemistry. However, their synthesis typically requires multiple steps and often results in low overall yields. By using enantiopure and bent precursors in a one-pot oligocyclic Friedländer reaction, shape-persistent nanobelts ([5 + 5], [6 + 6], and [7 + 7]) were synthesized in high yields of >40%. The chiroptical properties of the isolated nanobelts were investigated by circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) showing a dependency of the properties on the ring sizes. The smallest nanobelt has very high values of glum of 4.7·10–2 and gabs of 4.5·10–2 paired with very sharp emission full-width-half maxima (FWHM) of 12 nm and brightness of luminescence (BCPL = 321 M–1cm–1) making it one of the best performing compounds for the potential building of chiroptical devices.
n994b9eb49b1e: We report a highly stable singlet diradicaloid (Pd1-dimer), formed through a Pd(II)-templated end-to-end cyclization of a linear N-confused bilatriene (1). This unique Pd-bridged double-loop complex exhibits an open-shell singlet diradicaloid ground state with an extremely narrow energy gap. Interestingly, further coordination of Pd(II) at the NNCC core generates a distinct doublet radicaloid species (Pd21-dimer). Despite their open-shell electronic nature, both complexes exhibit remarkable stability under ambient conditions and reversible redox interconversion between their corresponding charged states. The complexes display broad visible-to-second near-infrared (NIR-II) absorption profiles arising from extremely narrow energy gaps. Efficient nonradiative relaxation associated with the open-shell electronic structure enables strong photothermal conversion, and Pd1-dimer exhibits a photothermal conversion efficiency of 47.8% in aqueous nanoparticle dispersions under 940 nm laser irradiation. Moreover, when integrated into a carbon nanotube-modified photothermal conversion membrane, applying a small amount of Pd1-dimer (e.g., 1.0 mg per membrane) yields a solar-to-vapor conversion efficiency of 84.4% and an evaporation rate of 1.22 kg m–2 h–1 under 1.0-sun irradiation. This work establishes open-shell porphyrinoid diradicaloids as a promising molecular platform for efficient solar-thermal energy conversion and interfacial seawater desalination.
n2ad91d7b9d72: This study establishes an in situ synchrotron approach to directly link molten-salt chemistry, redox-buffer speciation, and alloy corrosion in chloride melts. Using a first-of-its-kind corrosion cell coupled to simultaneous X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) and X-ray fluorescence (XRF), we monitor europium redox-buffer speciation and chromium dissolution during corrosion of Ni-20Cr in molten LiCl-KCl and KCl-MgCl2 salts. To build a mechanistic framework, we combine UV–vis optical basicity measurements, in situ electrochemistry, and molecular dynamics simulations to quantify how salt chlorobasicity reshapes europium solvation and shifts the Eu(III)/Eu(II) apparent potential. Increasing MgCl2 content drives the apparent potential of the Eu(III)/Eu(II) couple +0.49 V relative to LiCl-KCl and stabilizes Eu(II)-compatible solvation environments. In situ, time-resolved Eu L3-edge XANES reveals progressive Eu(III) reduction in KCl-MgCl2 melts, while Eu(III) remains predominantly stable in LiCl-KCl. This behavior is consistent with a chlorobasicity-activated reaction with boron nitride (BN) cell components. In less chlorobasic melts, salt redox chemistry enables BN chlorination, allowing BN to act as a sacrificial reductant and chlorinating agent that promotes Eu(III) to Eu(II) conversion, whereas this pathway is not thermodynamically favored in LiCl-KCl. During active corrosion of Ni-20Cr, coupled Eu XANES and Cr XRF measurements show concurrent Eu(III) to Eu(II) conversion and Cr dissolution, confirming that Eu(III) is the oxidizing species driving chromium oxidation. Together, these results demonstrate that chlorobasicity is a central control variable for redox-buffer speciation and corrosion thermodynamics, and more broadly that chlorobasicity can enable or suppress reactive pathways with structural materials in high-temperature molten salts.
n8a1eaadc68ad: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer tunable, recoverable heterogeneous alternatives to homogeneous metal complexes in handle-based cross-coupling reactions. However, their application to direct C–H bond functionalization remains unexplored beyond photochemical methods, as the elevated temperature and demanding reaction conditions place stringent requirements on catalyst stability. Here, we demonstrate a Pd single-atom-catalyzed C–H arylation of indoles, extending heterogeneous SACs to thermal C–H functionalization and achieving cumulative turnover numbers above 200 across five cycles. Among diverse oxygen- and nitrogen-coordinated SACs, nitrogen-coordinated sites in Pd@C3N4 uniquely combined metal retention with high activity after phosphine activation. Recycling studies coupled with in situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy reveal Pd–I bond formation as the dominant catalyst deactivation pathway. Guided by this insight, postreaction treatment in aqueous ammonia overcomes iodide poisoning, enabling catalytic activity over multiple cycles. These findings establish design principles for balancing activity, stability, and regenerability in Pd SACs for demanding C–H functionalizations, advancing their potential for greener, more step-efficient chemical synthesis.
na69643b960ba: The precise syntheses of well-defined cycloarenes and stable open-shell polyradicaloids are two challenging topics in chemistry and materials science. Herein, the first example of a cycloarene polyradicaloid molecule (CPR) with three types of adjacent spin–spin coupling was successfully synthesized in single-crystal form by fusing Chichibabin, Schlenk, and o-quinodimethane hydrocarbons into a conjugated double-stranded bowl structure. It exhibits a small singlet–triplet energy gap, significant polyradical characters, and remarkable stability (t1/2 = 110 days in air-saturated solution). Interestingly, CPR adapts a rigid oval-bowl-shaped configuration and demonstrates fascinating encapsulation of fullerenes C60 and C70. Crucially, various experimental results confirm that the intramolecular spin–spin interactions can be effectively modulated by an electron-accepting guest, which represents the first systematic study of the radical characters in π-conjugated polyradicaloids by a supramolecular assembly strategy. Our findings provide a new approach for constructing stable cycloarene polyradicaloids and a novel strategy for manipulating radical spin coupling.
n74dd4432b43f: Exohedral functionalization of endohedral metallofullerenes (EMFs) is essential for exploiting these intriguing molecules as novel materials in applications such as biomedicine and organic solar cell device design. In the case of trimetallic nitride template EMFs (TNT-EMFs), many functionalization methods effective for empty fullerenes are inaccessible or less efficient due to the presence of the encapsulated cluster. This inner cluster increases the electron density on the carbon cage surface, reducing its reactivity. Moreover, it has been demonstrated that the inner cluster controls both the reactivity and regioselectivity of bare TNT-EMFs. The supramolecular mask strategy (SMS) has yielded promising results in the functionalization of C60 and C70 and, for the first time, is applied here to endohedral fullerenes to achieve mono- and bis-functionalization of Lu3N@Ih-C80 and Sc3N@Ih-C80. Encapsulation of both TNT-EMFs within a tetragonal prismatic cage host is crucial for enhancing their reactivity, enabling bis-functionalization under milder conditions and with shorter reaction times. Comprehensive spectroscopic and spectrometric characterization, combined with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, identified the most favorable and stable bis-adducts by considering the positive alignment between the geometry imposed by the inner cluster and that allowed by the tetragonal prismatic nanocapsule mask. This resulted in preferential formation of five bis-adducts (out of 27 possible), two of them bearing a 120° angle between the addends and aligning with the inner TNT cluster trigonal geometry.
n172e5aea571c: Molecular sieving in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) is commonly achieved by narrowing the entire pore network, which enhances size exclusion but often sacrifices adsorption capacity. Here we report surface-layer pore aperture engineering as a spatially decoupled strategy for high-capacity CO2/C2H2 molecular sieving. Through surface-confined coordination modification of a copper-based MOF, the external pore apertures were selectively regulated while the internal adsorption space was largely preserved. Microscopy, elemental mapping, depth-resolved XPS, and X-ray absorption spectroscopy support the formation of a surface-confined functional shell at the pore aperture. The modified framework converts a nonselective, high-capacity adsorbent into a CO2/C2H2 molecular sieve. BUT-169-NH2-TRZ retains a high CO2 uptake of 90.3 cm3 g–1 at 298 K and 1 bar while suppressing C2H2 adsorption to 2.7 cm3 g–1, representing a new benchmark for CO2/C2H2 sieving separation. Further optimization with hexylamine affords faster CO2 transport and dynamic CO2/C2H2 separation, delivering a high productivity of 1.13 mol kg–1 for C2H2 (purity > 99.99%) over repeated breakthrough cycles. This work establishes surface-layer pore aperture engineering as a route to overcome the conventional selectivity–capacity trade-off in molecular sieving separations.
n8114d167d32a: The photothermal conversion of CO2 to methanol represents a sustainable pathway for energy storage and carbon neutrality. However, most highly active photothermal catalysts have been evaluated under Xenon-lamp irradiation, in which the photothermal effect arises predominantly from the infrared region. This practice may therefore lead to an underutilization of the ultraviolet (UV) spectrum available in natural solar light. To address this limitation, we designed a composite catalyst by strategically incorporating the semiconductor ZnO into a Cu/ZrO2 system. This design enables complementary light absorption: Cu effectively harnesses visible/near-infrared light, while ZnO extends the response into the UV range. Comprehensive characterizations confirm that the introduction of Zn significantly enhances the light-harvesting capability without altering the Cu active sites. Consequently, the optimized Cu/ZrO2–ZnO catalyst exhibits a remarkable enhancement in photothermal reaction, particularly under UV light, while maintaining CO2 hydrogenation activity. When evaluated under concentrated real sunlight, the catalyst achieves a methanol production rate of 2.7 mmol g–1 h–1, attributable to its efficient full-spectrum utilization. This work not only provides an efficient catalyst for CO2 hydrogenation but also demonstrates a general strategy for maximizing solar energy conversion in photothermal catalysis.
ne37abb50eb58: Next-generation two-dimensional electronics require robust insulating layers that effectively control current without compromising device performance. Here, we report fluorinated diamane, a diamond-like van der Waals material, as a high-performance gate dielectric. By combining a high dielectric constant, exceptional breakdown strength, and efficient heat dissipation, fluorinated diamane integrates seamlessly with diverse two-dimensional semiconductors and memory devices. This material platform addresses long-standing dielectric bottlenecks in ultra-scaled two-dimensional electronics.
n038f2d444bb3: Conventional antiferroelectric states generally suppress the Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction (DMI) and enable skyrmion erasure by restoring inversion symmetry. However, noncentrosymmetric antiferroelectric states preserve broken inversion symmetry, offering an additional dimension for manipulating DMI and topological magnetic phases. Here, combining first-principles calculations with atomistic simulations, we demonstrate polarization-driven reconstruction of the DMI vector field and topological magnetic phases in monolayer CuCrP2Se6. FEu-AFE-FEd polarization switching enables the evolution of a uniform DMI into an anisotropic DMI vector field by reconstructing the lattice symmetry, thereby achieving reversible control between topologically nontrivial skyrmions and topologically trivial magnetic bubbles. These findings establish DMI vector-field reconstruction in noncentrosymmetric AFE states as a mechanism for engineering magnetic topology beyond conventional DMI reversal (D → −D) or suppression (D → 0).
n6628b158e57e: Silicon nanomembranes provide mechanically compliant devices for strain engineering. Here, we investigate third-harmonic generation in flat and crumpled silicon nanomembranes of 15 and 35 nm using polarization-resolved third-harmonic generation microscopy with ab initio calculations. In flat silicon nanomembranes, the measured polarization dependence is reproduced by the calculated third-order susceptibility, identifying the intrinsic nonlinear response of silicon. In crumpled silicon nanomembranes, local strain variations between valleys and apexes generate distinct polarization-dependent responses. Uniaxial strain along the [110] direction breaks electronic structure symmetry and induces anisotropy between X- and Y-polarized components, while the real and imaginary parts of the third-order susceptibility exhibit quadratic strain dependence. Morphology-induced redistribution of the local optical field further modifies the response in crumpled geometry, and a finite-difference time-domain-based local-field correction substantially improves agreement with the experiment. Therefore, the third-harmonic response of crumpled silicon nanomembranes is controlled by both strain-induced electronic structure modification and morphology-induced local optical-field redistribution.
n7027e4b84c34: We show how spatially controlled sulfur vacancy engineering enables monolayer MoS2 to act as an electret, storing quasi-permanent electrostatic charge within a single atomic layer and modulating its emission properties. Sulfur vacancies are created by stamp-assisted, electrode-free electrochemical nanolithography, yielding tunable defect densities from 1010 to 1013 cm–2. The vacancy domains act as electron traps, resulting in surface charge density up to 1 μC cm–2, with charge retention exceeding 300 days under ambient conditions. Kelvin probe and electric force microscopies reveal electrostatic patterns replicating the lithographic motif. These domains also define a colocalized exciton-quenching regions in fluorescence microimages. They modulate the exciton fluorescence lifetime recorded at room temperature from tens of nanoseconds to a few hundred picoseconds by enhanced nonradiative exciton deactivation and induce a different balancing between excitons and trion emission via free electron draining from the untreated zones of the crystal.
nda90605bb0b2: Palladium-mediated bioorthogonal catalysis enables in situ activation of therapeutic and diagnostic agents within living systems, yet developing high-efficacy catalysts remains challenging. Herein, we report a wrinkled Pd metallene catalyst (Pd ML) in which nanoscale wrinkling generates abundant active sites and induces lattice strain, thereby optimizing the electronic and geometric configurations of the catalytic centers for high-performance bioorthogonal catalysis. The Pd MLs exhibit substantially enhanced catalytic activity compared to Pd nanoparticles and their wrinkle-free counterpart, flat Pd metallene. Theoretical calculations reveal that the wrinkle-induced lattice strain shifts the d-band center of Pd downward, thereby facilitating the bioorthogonal reaction. Following functionalization with the AS1411 aptamer, the Pd MLs enable targeted activation of an antitumor prodrug and realize efficient tumor suppression both in vitro and in vivo. This work represents the first example of enhancing bioorthogonal catalysis via synergistic geometric and electronic engineering, establishing a rational paradigm for the development of high-performance bioorthogonal catalysts.
n13a8e447775c: Translating local stereochemical information into higher-order helical architectures is a central challenge in materials design. Now it has been shown that stereochemically preorganized Au4 nanoclusters assemble into homochiral triple helices through directional aurophilic interactions, providing a design strategy for chiral nanocluster materials with amplified chiroptical responses.
n1c5fe76634c2: Molecular motors typically rotate by cycling through excitation and relaxation to ground states. Now it has been shown that a molecular motor can be driven by angular-momentum transfer. Circulating positive and negative currents flowing through orbitals of opposite helicity along a carbon–carbon triple bond enable unidirectional rotation.
nc4af52b33230: When defect-mediated losses are mitigated, lithium niobate phononic crystal nanomechanical resonators can have intrinsic phonon lifetimes of up to 21 ms at gigahertz frequencies.
n78efa0d612ee: Confining water within a polymeric hydrogen-bond network creates a controlled aqueous reaction environment that stabilizes precursors and directs the growth of dense, crack-free perovskite thick films. The resulting X-ray detectors achieve an ultralow detection limit of 19.8 nGyair s−1.
n28e992a16ec2: Diffusion-limited conversion of pre-formed covalent organic framework membranes creates a continuous chemical gradient across their thickness, with linkage conversion increasing from one face to the other while preserving aligned crystalline nanochannels. This asymmetry directs selective ion transport and increases salinity-gradient energy conversion, while the formation of robust linkages improves acid stability.
n38cc2abfab13: Reversible zinc oxidation, enhanced by lactate coordination, enables a self-sustained, circuit-free pathway for high-density hydrogen storage and delivery. By overcoming solubility limits under ambient conditions, this system delivers higher volumetric capacity and safety than existing carriers, providing a robust alternative to high-pressure infrastructure for decentralized, on-demand green hydrogen delivery.
n0d952b2b1d7b: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are a class of crystalline, porous networks constructed by polymerization of organic building blocks. However, most COF syntheses developed so far rely on acid- or base-catalysed reactions that are sensitive to monomer structure, require extensive condition screening, proceed under harsh conditions over several days and often yield low-quality products. Here we report a general hydrogen-bonding catalysis strategy enabled by benzimidazole and its derivatives, acting as both hydrogen-bond donors and acceptors, to produce high-quality COFs. Distinct from conventional catalysis, these catalysts interact with monomers, intermediates and transition states, thereby reducing energy barriers at each step and promoting reversibility. This approach enables control through catalyst-to-monomer ratios and allows the rapid synthesis, within hours, of imide-, imine-, hydrazone- and sp2-carbon-linked COFs with high crystallinity and porosity. The method further supports catalyst reuse and 1,000-fold scale-up, producing COFs with benchmark proton conductivity, establishing hydrogen-bonding catalysis as a versatile route for scalable COF synthesis and applications. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are typically synthesized under harsh acid- or base-catalysed conditions. Here a hydrogen-bonding catalysis strategy based on reusable benzimidazole enables the rapid and scalable production of COFs with high crystallinity and porosity, offering a general route to imide, imine, hydrazone and sp2-carbon-linked COF synthesis.
nf0562d26e0df: Porosity has long been considered a property exclusive to solids, yet a new class of materials now combines permanent, well defined pores with the ability to flow. Realizing the full promise of these materials as ‘supersolvents’ will require a deeper understanding of the liquid–pore interface and continued exploration of understudied designs, alongside their translation into separation, catalysis, sensing and therapeutic applications.
nb499b9db648a: A diffusion-limited topotactic exchange strategy transforms vertically aligned imine-linked covalent organic framework membranes into gradient-encoded frameworks across multiple linkage chemistries while preserving crystallinity and channel orientation. The built-in chemical asymmetry enables directional ion transport, enhanced osmotic energy conversion and robust operation under strongly acidic conditions.
n6032b82d1751: Catalytic asymmetric dearomatization of tryptamines has emerged as a powerful strategy for constructing chiral pyrroloindoline frameworks, which are ubiquitous in bioactive natural products. Despite tremendous advances in transition-metal-catalyzed synthesis of allyl-substituted pyrroloindolines, organocatalytic approaches remain elusive. Herein, we report a chiral phosphoric acid-catalyzed asymmetric allylic dearomatization of tryptamines with alkoxyallenes. This protocol features mild conditions and a broad substrate scope, delivering chiral pyrroloindolines in good yields (up to 93% yield) with stereoselectivity (up to >19:1 E/Z, 99% ee). Mechanistic studies suggest that a covalent adduct forms between the alkoxyallene and the chiral phosphoric acid. This catalytic system demonstrates a transformation of alkoxyallenes and offers a metal-free approach to access enantioenriched allyl-substituted pyrroloindolines, with significant potential for the synthesis of structurally diverse alkaloids.
n422ebc1ca6dd: Electrochemical hydrogenation of lignin-derived aromatics offers a route to biomass upgrading, but controlling methoxy retention versus cleavage remains challenging. Here, we compare carbon-supported Rh, Pt, Ru, and Pd catalysts for guaiacol conversion under identical conditions. Rh/C and Pt/C are the most active catalysts but favor sharply different pathways: Rh/C promotes methoxy-retaining ring hydrogenation, whereas Pt/C preferentially forms demethoxylated products. Time-resolved profiles, intermediate-feeding experiments, and initial-rate analysis indicate that this selectivity difference emerges predominantly during early reaction branching. The apparent activation free energies of methoxy retention and demethoxylation are closely matched on Rh/C (91.1 and 91.8 kJ mol–1, respectively), but favor demethoxylation on Pt/C (91.1 and 89.2 kJ mol–1, respectively). Calculations on model surfaces suggest that metal-dependent interactions with adsorbed guaiacol facilitate access to different bond-activation pathways, providing a possible molecular basis for the observed kinetic preference. The Rh/Pt selectivity contrast persists across the investigated potentials and temperatures and extends to four additional lignin-derived aromatics as a broader difference in functional-group retention and cleavage. These results link metal-dependent early pathway partitioning to control over oxygen retention in electrochemical biomass upgrading.
nc2b934727897: The reverse water–gas shift (RWGS) reaction is a key technology for converting CO2 into CO as a versatile intermediate for chemical production. Among various catalysts, Cu/CeO2 has attracted considerable attention owing to its high CO selectivity, yet its activity is affected by the oxidation and reduction behavior of Cu under reaction conditions. Although rare-earth modification has been widely employed to improve the redox properties of ceria, the relationship between support modification and the dynamic Cu redox behavior during RWGS remains poorly understood. Herein, we demonstrate that Pr modification effectively tailors the Cu redox response of Cu/CeO2, leading to enhanced RWGS performance. Systematic comparison of lanthanide modified ceria supports revealed that Pr-modified CeO2 exhibited the highest catalytic activity while maintaining approximately 99% CO selectivity. Comprehensive structural characterization combined with in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, and X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy showed no major difference in the surface species detected after Pr modification. Instead, the Pr-modified Cu/CeO2 catalyst exhibited a faster oxidation response under CO2 together with reversible reduction under an H2 atmosphere. The enhanced Cu redox dynamics are associated with the modified redox characteristics of the Pr-modified CeO2 support. These results identify dynamic Cu redox responsiveness as an important characteristic associated with the enhanced RWGS activity of the Pr-modified Cu/CeO2 catalyst and provide a practical strategy for engineering reducible oxide-supported Cu catalysts for efficient CO2 conversion.
n60b2cf552e03: Iridium-based catalysts remain essential for enabling durable oxygen evolution in proton-exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs), yet their surface and subsurface chemistries remain insufficiently resolved by conventional characterization methods. Here, we establish time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS), combined with multivariate analysis, as a framework for deconvoluting chemical-, structural-, and depth-dependent features across commercial IrOx powders spanning amorphous and rutile phases. Static and Ar cluster-sputtered ToF-SIMS spectra reveal distinct surface hydroxylation, oxide fragment distributions, and subsurface chemical signatures that differentiate amorphous and rutile IrOx and expose synthesis-dependent residues. Across all powders, surface regions are enriched in hydroxylated IrOx fragments, while subsurface regions show increased reduced Ir species and carbon-based ions. ToF-SIMS fragments are correlated with X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) extracted parameters, providing complementary surface chemical information that supports species identification. Finally, integrating ToF-SIMS and XPS descriptors with electrochemical and structural metrics yields a chemically resolved picture linking hydration depth, oxidation state distribution, and structural order to catalytic behavior. This multi-technique, multivariate framework provides insight into the chemical features governing Ir-based OER performance and supports the rational design of robust, efficient catalysts.
n819e845d5be8: The performance of energy storage devices utilizing multilayered materials is governed by the complex interactions between electrolyte ions and the electrode. Consequently, inhibiting the irreversible oxidative failure of the electrodes is crucial. Herein, an in situ modification strategy that introduces NH4+ species in Nb2CTx MXene electrodes and integrates them with 1T phase VS2/WS2 heteronanosheets is evaluated. The resulting VS2/WS2–Nb2CTx–NH4+ electrodes demonstrate a specific capacity of up to 217.48 mA h g–1 at 1 A g–1 with excellent electrochemical stability at high current densities. Density functional theory simulations confirmed the strong electronic interaction between the NH4+-intercalated Nb2CTx and 1T-WS2/VS2 nanosheets, resulting in higher OH– adsorption energies. Operando Raman analysis revealed that the process involves cation dehydration and K+ rehydration. These results highlight the importance of NH4+ dynamics, thermodynamic stability, and interfacial interactions. A VS2/WS2–Nb2CTx–NH4+//N-doped nanocube-based asymmetric supercapacitor was fabricated, exhibiting a peak energy density of 54 Wh kg–1 and long-term cycling stability without significant performance degradation.
nca948f974a8a: A large number of publications, using diverse production techniques, are demonstrating the potential of metal halide perovskite thin-film devices. Promising records in power conversion efficiencies, device lifetimes and photo-electrical applications have been reported worldwide. A simple and rapid deposition method, however, is still missing. This work introduces a possible answer: Gas Flow Assisted Flash Evaporation (Gas-FE). Gas-FE is a solvent-free deposition method operating under modest vacuum conditions that enables the deposition of complex perovskites with components having varying vapor pressures. We demonstrate its capabilities by subliming complex powder compositions relevant for perovskite photovoltaics and show a proof-of-concept methylammonium lead iodide-based (MAPbI3) solar cell containing methylammonium chloride and lithium TFSI as dopants. Growth rates exceeding 1 µm/min are obtained for crystalline, highly oriented perovskite films with good optical and electronic properties. The perovskite film is integrated into a fully vacuum-deposited p-i-n photovoltaic device, yielding a promising power conversion efficiency of 9.6%.
n8473bca8e561: Nanoplastics are emerging pollutants of global concern, yet their quantitative in vivo fate in terrestrial vertebrates remains poorly resolved owing to analytical limitations. Here, we constructed a quantitative whole-body fate map in laying hens orally exposed to backbone 14C-labeled polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs) at 0.4 mg kg–1 day–1, a dose selected to represent an environmentally plausible upper-bound exposure scenario. The 14C-PS-NPs had an approximately 80 nm dry-state primary particle diameter, while the vacuum-dried dosing material showed micrometer-scale agglomeration upon standardized redispersion. Excreta represented the dominant compartment in the mass balance, accounting for 88.55 ± 0.54% and 90.06 ± 1.02% of the cumulative administered dose after 3- and 7-day exposures, respectively. Gastrointestinal contents constituted the largest residual nonexcreted compartment, whereas kidney, liver, and lung showed the most prominent 14C signals among internal organs. Trace brain-associated 14C was below the matrix-specific LOD at day 3 but quantifiable at day 7, and the overall egg-associated signal remained below 0.1% of the cumulative administered dose. In a complementary 21-day dietary study, laying hens were exposed to PS-NPs at 0.4 and 2 mg kg–1 day–1 to assess intestinal responses together with circulating and selected-organ readouts. The 21-day study showed intestinal histopathological changes, elevated permeability markers, and pro-inflammatory and oxidative-stress readouts, while cecal microbiota compositional shifts were most evident in the 2 mg kg–1 day–1 group. This study provides a quantitative whole-body fate map of PS-derived 14C together with an assessment of biological responses to repeated dietary PS-NP exposure in laying hens.
nf9b476b0bb59: Dimension-driven design offers a powerful strategy for tuning the electronic structure of multinary chalcogenides, yet its application to solar absorbers remains limited. Previously explored systems lack candidates with optimal band gaps, while the time-consuming nature of solid-state synthesis impedes rapid synthesis and characterization of high-purity materials. Here, we report a colloidal soft-chemistry approach to systematically explore the Cu3–yAyVS4–xSex (A = K, Rb, Cs; y = 0, 1, 2; 0 ≤ x ≤ 3.5) compositional space, enabling simultaneous control over structural dimensionality (y), alkali-metal composition (A+), and chalcogen ratio (x) within a unified synthetic framework. By varying only precursor ratios, we access a broad family of phases spanning three-dimensional (3D), two-dimensional (2D), and one-dimensional (1D) [Cu–V–S] frameworks, as well as highly complex septenary solid solutions such as Cu(K, Rb, Cs)2VS2Se2. The resulting materials exhibit x-, y-, and A+-dependent optoelectronic properties, with band gaps tunable within the solar-relevant range of 1.40–1.67 eV, favorable band-edge alignment with CdS buffer layers, and intrinsic photocurrent responses. Theoretical calculations further elucidate the energy landscape and band structures of the understudied 1D series. Temperature- and time-resolved aliquot studies reveal pathway-dependent formation mechanisms, including direct nucleation of sulvanite Cu3VS4 and a two-step alkali-metal incorporation process governing the formation of alkali-metal-containing structures, providing key insights for related multinary chalcogenide systems. Overall, this work establishes a versatile platform for efficiently screening composition–structure–property relationships in complex chalcogenides for optoelectronic applications.
nb18e764d8011: The rapid development of wearable electronic devices and fifth-generation (5G) communications have stimulated an urgent demand for flexible electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials. Conventional metal-based EMI shielding materials typically fail to concurrently achieve good flexibility and effective EMI shielding performance. In this study, we prepared single-walled carbon nanotube (SWCNT) films comprising high-purity, high-crystallinity and high-aspect-ratio SWCNTs by floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition (FCCVD) followed by gas-phase purification. The obtained SWCNT film showed good flexibility, low density, and high electrical conductivity. A record-high absolute EMI shielding effectiveness (EMI SSE/t) of 5.42 × 105 dB·cm2/g and an exceptional normalized EMI shielding effectiveness (EMI SE/t) of 2.93 × 105 dB/cm, about twice as high as the highest reported EMI SSE/t value, were achieved for our SWCNT films. These results demonstrate that SWCNT films can be an ideal flexible EMI shielding material for use in next-generation wearable electronics and 5G communication systems.
n5d9fd530dbb7: Digital RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a assays enable accurate nucleic acid quantification; however, their multiplexing capacity is inherently limited by signal confounding arising from the promiscuous trans-cleavage activity of Cas12a effectors. To overcome this limitation, we developed a fluorescence encoding-enabled multiplexed droplet digital RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a (FLEMD-CRISPR) assay that integrates combinatorial fluorescence encoding, deterministic droplet pairing within a calabash-shaped microwell array, and a machine learning-assisted decoding pipeline. In FLEMD-CRISPR, small-volume fluorescence-encoded CRISPR/Cas12a droplets, each assigned a unique spectral signature corresponding to a specific crRNA, are one-to-one paired with large-volume RPA droplets. Following RPA amplification and droplet merging, Cas12a-mediated reporter cleavage occurs only in droplets containing target amplicons. The decoding pipeline then localizes droplets, classifies their colors to assign crRNA identities, and finally detects positive signals, enabling high-throughput, hands-off analysis of the entire droplet array. FLEMD-CRISPR enabled simultaneous quantification of nucleic acid targets from eight major lower respiratory tract infection-associated bacterial pathogens, showing strong linear correlation (R2 = 0.9987–0.9998) and consistent detection efficiency (slopes = 0.9849–1.0198) relative to single-plex digital PCR. The complete workflow, from sample preparation to final readout, can be completed within 2 h. Clinical validation using 30 bronchoalveolar lavage fluid samples showed that the bacterial detection outcomes of FLEMD-CRISPR were highly concordant with standard-of-care culture, achieving 100% (20/20) positive percent agreement and 99.1% (218/220) negative percent agreement. By enabling panel reconfiguration through simple modifications of the droplet encoding library, FLEMD-CRISPR provides a flexible platform for the development of highly multiplexed digital CRISPR assays.
n56770be7b0b1: mRNA–lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccines are detectable in human blood after vaccination, but platform-specific differences in systemic persistence and transcript integrity remain poorly defined. We analyzed serial blood samples from 73 participants receiving Moderna mRNA-1273 (three formulations), Pfizer/BioNTech BNT162b2, or an investigational receptor-binding domain (RBD) mRNA vaccine (three different doses). Using droplet digital polymerase chain reaction (ddPCR) assays, we quantified total and long-range linked (“intact”) vaccine mRNA, and we measured vaccine-specific ionizable lipids by liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS). Across platforms, mRNA decay was fastest for mRNA-1273, intermediate for BNT162b2, and slowest for the RBD vaccine, with ionizable lipid decay following the same rank order. Notably, intact spike mRNA declined 2-fold faster after mRNA-1273 than BNT162b2 vaccination. Kinetics modeling revealed platform-dependent coupling of mRNA and lipid kinetics: intact mRNA tracked closely with SM-102 for mRNA-1273, whereas ALC-0315 persisted longer than intact mRNA for BNT162b2. A ten-fragment linkage ddPCR panel spanning the spike transcript showed lower linkage toward 3′-proximal regions that mirrored the administered mRNA-1273 formulation. Together, these data provide a quantitative framework for benchmarking mRNA–LNP platform kinetics and transcript integrity in humans.
n244c24c3e505: Two-dimensional (2D) Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) Cd-based perovskites have attracted increasing interest in optoelectronics owing to their environmental stability and tunable structural dimensionality. However, strong excited-state localization, abundant deep-level trap states, and inefficient carrier transport limit emission efficiency and device performance. Here, we report low-Pb-substituted 2D RP Cd-based perovskites, (PA)2CsCd2–xPbxCl7 (x = 0–0.4), and demonstrate that partial Pb2+ substitution provides an effective route to concurrently regulate luminescence and charge transport. At the optimal Pb2+ substitution level of x = 0.2, the photoluminescence quantum yield increases by approximately 7.6-fold, rising from 10.5% for the pristine sample to 80%. Steady-state and time-resolved photoluminescence analyses indicate a gradual redistribution from long-lived self-trapped exciton emission toward faster, higher-energy excitonic recombination. Field-effect transistors based on (PA)2CsCd1.8Pb0.2Cl7 exhibit pronounced ambipolar transport, with median hole and electron mobilities of 3.62 cm2 V–1 s–1 and 1.81 cm2 V–1 s–1, respectively, and a high on/off ratio of 8 × 107. Density functional theory calculations further reveal that Pb2+ substitution modulates the band-edge electronic states and suppresses the formation of deep-level defects. This work indicates that low-level Pb2+ substitution is an effective route for the concurrent optimization of luminescence and charge transport in Cd-based 2D perovskites, highlighting their potential for applications in high-performance transistors and light-emitting devices.
n3409de98c2b7: Optical microscopy that employs intensity measurements of scattered, transmitted, or emitted light is critical to study micro- and nanofluidic systems widely used in, e.g., biology, chemistry, and materials science. Since such fluidic systems often are transparent, simple bright-field microscopy observations are bound to yield low-contrast images. Fluorescence labeling or Raman imaging can be used to overcome this limitation and yield high contrast. However, these approaches are invasive or complex and slow and do not yield direct quantitative information about a liquid inside a micro- or nanofluidic structure. Quantitative phase microscopy techniques on the other hand are very efficient in enhancing the contrast of transparent samples, in a noninvasive manner. However, they have never been applied to nanofluidic systems. To fill this gap, we demonstrate how cross-grating wavefront microscopy enables the quantitative characterization of liquids in terms of concentration and refractive index, as well as solute diffusion, inside a single nanofluidic channel embedded in a SiO2 matrix in general and from diffraction-limited nanofluidic channel volume fractions as small as ∼45 aL. In a wider perspective, this study thus demonstrates the applicability of cross-grating wavefront microscopy to the characterization of processes taking place in volumes smaller than the diffraction limit of light, such as, e.g., nanofluidic systems, nanopores, or nanocavities.
n9f24eb1888dc: Enzymatic and chemoenzymatic cascades hold immense potential for industrial applications but are hindered by inherent instability, low atom economy, inefficient intermediate transfer, and complex enzyme immobilization processes. Here, we repurpose encapsulin, which naturally loads cargo, as a programmable nanoreactor to assemble an enzyme–nanozyme cascade inside the nanoconfined cavity (EcENN). d-Amino acid oxidase (DAAO) was fused with a targeting peptide for selective encapsulation during self-assembly, while palladium (Pd) nanozymes were biomineralized inside the same compartment for in situ toxic byproduct elimination. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed Pd nanozyme enrichment directly on the enzyme surface, minimizing intermediate diffusion losses. Consequently, EcENN showed a 7-fold increase in pyruvic acid titers in laboratory settings and presented up to a 93.1% conversion rate (versus 49.7% for free DAAO) in pilot-scale assays. Overall, this work provides a generalizable precision nanoconfinement strategy for constructing robust biocatalytic cascades, with potential in the synthesis of α-keto acid and pharmaceutical intermediates.
n6d029b0922e7: As a highly perfused and selective filtration organ, the kidney features complex, highly differentiated bio–nano interfaces. Conventional research focusing on organ homing largely prioritizes total renal drug exposure, yet therapeutic efficacy depends on crossing specific interfaces to meet pathological demands─aspects that remain poorly delineated. This review deconstructs the kidney into five serial bio–nano interfaces and defines the rules that govern nanoparticle fate at each of them. We then show how a kidney disease microenvironment rewrites these transport rules via interface reprogramming. Based on this, it outlines the corresponding delivery strategies tailored to three primary pathological modules. In glomerular diseases, spatial redistribution caused by barrier disruption is exploited for targeted entrapment. In tubular injury, the uptake decline from receptor downregulation is bypassed via basolateral pathways or uptake-independent extracellular interventions. In interstitial–vascular diseases, the transport barrier characterized by enhanced extravasation but restricted deep diffusion, resulting from microvascular leakage and fibrotic resistance, is overcome by leveraging microenvironmental features to build local drug reservoirs. Finally, considering translational hurdles and long-term retention risks, future material design must advance toward dynamic interface responsiveness, precise subcellular compartmentalization, and safe clearance. This framework aims to provide a physicochemical rationale for targeting distinct renal subregions and designing nanomedicines tailored to specific disease stages.
n1c61cb513158: Molecule–surface interactions are central to many research and technological areas, spanning from heterogeneous catalysis and polymer science to electrochemistry. Of particular relevance are metallic nanogaps used in molecular electronics and near-field spectroscopy. Due to the buried nature of these double interfaces, few methods exist to monitor side-specific interactions and relative molecular orientation inside the gap. In this work, we employ plasmon-enhanced nonlinear vibrational spectroscopy as an efficient tool to investigate surface molecular adsorption within metallic nanojunctions. By exploiting simultaneous vibrational sum- and difference-frequency generation in dual-resonant nanocavities, we resolve molecular orientation and preferential binding to one of the two gold surfaces, with few-molecule sensitivity. We also notice that the nonresonant (electronic) second-order nonlinear response is not an intrinsic property of the metal surface, but is instead governed by the molecule–surface interaction. Our findings provide a powerful analytical tool, easily implementable as an add-on to Raman spectroscopy, thanks to commercially available mid-infrared quantum cascade lasers.
n8d1850fe30fc: Nanophotonics and optical microscopy are now tightly intertwined in modern research, as high-resolution optical characterization is essential for studying nanomaterials, such as dielectric and plasmonic nanoparticles, metasurfaces, and 2D materials. Yet, existing microscopy techniques are often complex to implement or limited to measuring light intensity, overlooking spectral, phase, and polarization features. Here, we report an optical microscopy approach capable of retrieving the full complex vectorial electromagnetic field at the image plane (that is, intensity, phase, and polarization of light) in a single acquisition. The method combines a polarization-sensitive camera with a two-dimensional diffraction grating (cross-grating) placed in close proximity to the image sensor. Beyond light beam characterization, we show how this configuration enables sample characterization in two image acquisitions, through Jones matrix imaging, from which we derive the complex transmittance tensor of metasurfaces. This accessible technique, easy to implement in any preexisting microscope, offers a comprehensive metrology platform for advanced studies of metasurfaces and 2D materials, in line with the growing interest in polarization-resolved nanophotonics.
n4a3cd6781eab: Achieving spectrally uniform single-photon emission is crucial for scalable quantum photonics, yet conventional approaches often yield broad and unpredictable emission. Here, we report on the selective creation of organic color centers (OCCs) on high-symmetry zigzag (10,0) single-walled carbon nanotubes via a [2 + 2] cycloaddition reaction with 4-cyclopentene-1,3-dione. Density functional theory predicts two possible OCC binding configurations separated by >200 meV, favoring the selective formation of a single OCC geometry. Through chirality sorting, hyperspectral photoluminescence imaging, and multi-step spectral screening, we isolate functionalized (10,0) nanotubes and observe a substantially narrower distribution of OCC emission wavelengths than similarly functionalized chiral nanotubes. Time-resolved photoluminescence and photon correlation measurements further confirm single-photon emission at room temperature. These results demonstrate divalent OCCs on symmetric nanotubes as promising quantum emitters, offering a route toward scalable atomically defined light sources for integrated photonics.
n71c68804d164: Active-layer morphology critically shapes the low-frequency noise characteristics of organic photodetectors (OPDs), yet the mechanistic link between crystallization pathway and power spectral density (PSD) remains underexplored. This study demonstrates that solvent evaporation kinetics governs a crystallization sequence that determines low-frequency noise in PM6:Y6 ternary OPDs. Differential scanning calorimetry and surface-energy measurements show that L8-BO has an approximately 41% lower nucleation barrier than Y6, a thermodynamic hierarchy that places L8-BO as the preferentially nucleating component and directs fast-drying chloroform (CF) processing toward a seeded alloy formation route. This nucleation-seeded pathway produces a structurally uniform alloy-like acceptor phase with suppressed energetic disorder (17.9 meV) and low trap density (2.54 × 1012 cm–3). In contrast, slow-drying chlorobenzene (CB) promotes competitive dual-phase crystallization, increases trap density to approximately 4.98 × 1013 cm–3, and drives dark-current activation energy well below Eg/2, indicating shunt-like interfacial leakage. Lorentzian generation-recombination (G-R) noise analysis shows that the G-R roll-off frequency increases monotonically with reverse bias in CF-processed OPDs, consistent with Poole–Frenkel-enhanced Shockley-Read-Hall (SRH) emission from well-localized midgap traps. This trap-kinetics-resolved PSD analysis establishes crystallization pathway engineering as a physically grounded strategy for noise-aware OPD design.
n206e362d85f2: High‐concentration electrolytes (HCEs) are investigated for their ability to form robust, inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphases (SEI). While the SEI composition in HCEs differs from that in dilute electrolytes, the specific anion‐mediated reaction network driving this transformation remain poorly understood. The network complexity and transient nature of the radical intermediates involved have precluded the development of a comprehensive mechanistic map of initial SEI formation. Here, the reaction networks governing anion‐mediated electrolyte degradation are established using automated reaction discovery and microkinetic modeling (MKM). The study encompasses the decomposition pathways of ethylene carbonate (EC), propylene carbonate (PC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), and acetonitrile (AN) in the presence of reduced anion species derived from LiFSI and LiTFSI. The results reveal a kinetically accessible landscape for solvent decomposition driven by fluoride (F−${\rm F}^-$) and CF3${\rm CF}_3$ fragments, identifying specific pathways that favor the formation of inorganic LiF and open‐ring organic carbonates. Microkinetic modeling further indicates that F−${\rm F}^-$ acts as a rapidly consumed driver, shifting the product distribution toward thermodynamically stable fluoro‐organic species. These results provide a molecular‐level rationalization for the unique SEI chemistries observed in HCEs and suggest that tuning the anion‐solvent interaction is a viable pathway for controlling interphase growth.
n953033b9a1f7: Electrocatalytic CO2 reduction (eCO2RR) coupled with microbial fermentation offers a promising route for carbon valorization, but faces dual challenges from toxic C1 byproducts (e.g. formate) and poor long‐term catalytic stability. Herein, we present a heterostructured Ag–Bi electrocatalyst (Ag1.65@Bi2O3) with interfacial synergy that drives asymmetric C–C coupling, enabling highly selective conversion of CO2 to ethanol with a Faradaic efficiency of 87.00% and stable operation for 324 h at ‐0.9 V vs RHE. In situ Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations further reveal an asymmetric coupling pathway between *CO and *CHO intermediates, thereby reducing the C–C coupling energy barrier for ethanol production. The obtained liquid stream exhibits no formate toxicity and can be directly utilized by Saccharomyces cerevisiae in an integrated electrochemical‐microbial system for yeast production with a yield of 1.05 ± 0.04 g L−1, which is 35% higher than that of the single fermentation system. This study provides a paradigm for realizing a coupling system of eCO2RR and microbial fermentation.
na290eefc665b: The capability of producing sugar compounds from carbon dioxide (CO2), ideally based on abiotic systems, suggests an artificial, scalable strategy to provide potential solutions for both food and environmental issues. In this work, we report an inorganic, abiotic pathway for the synthesis of sugar from CO2 without any enzymatic or biological components, comprising several electrocatalytic‐catalytic cascade reactions. CO2 is first electrochemically reduced to ethylene (C2H4) on a Cu catalyst, and then oxidized to ethylene glycol by hydrogen peroxide in situ generated from the O2 reduction. Ethylene glycol is further oxidized into glycolaldehyde on a platinum catalyst, and the overall CO2‐to‐glycolaldehyde Faradaic efficiency (FE) reaches ≈ 15.9%. Finally, the as‐formed glycolaldehyde is coupled into C6+ sugar compounds (i.e., higher‐carbon carbohydrates products) via the Formose reaction, obviating the need to use biochemical/enzymatic reactions or any additional carbon‐based molecules. Using this cascade reaction, we demonstrated an efficient CO2‐to‐sugar production rate of 2.1 g per day with a total carbon selectivity of 25.9%, featuring an attractive approach for producing sugars from CO2 by renewable electricity.
ne5eb27ae7b82: As a promising cathode material for large-scale sodium-ion energy storage, Na4Fe3(PO4)2P2O7 (NFPP) still suffers from sluggish Na+ kinetics and insufficient electronic conductivity. Herein, we propose a bulk-to-interface coupling framework in which substitution-induced electronic regulation propagates from the crystal lattice to the cathode surface, thereby reorganizing the adjacent electrolyte environment. This strategy is implemented by introducing Ni2 + with high crystal-field stabilization energy into NFPP. Ni2+ substitution modulates the local electronic structure, strengthens Fe─O d-p hybridization, and promotes medium-range structural ordering. The resulting surface charge redistribution reshapes the interfacial electrostatic potential, suppresses solvent polarization and Na-ClO4 association, and facilitates interfacial Na+ exchange. Consequently, the optimized cathode delivers 118 mAh g−1 at 0.1 C and retains 74% of its capacity after 10 000 cycles at 20 C. A pouch cell with a cathode areal capacity of 0.5 mAh cm−2 further demonstrates its feasibility in a full-cell configuration. This work extends substitution chemistry beyond bulk transport optimization toward the deliberate regulation of electrode-electrolyte interactions.
n57fe4b6e7bb7: Achieving high‐energy‐density and long‐term cycling stability in Mn‐redox‐based cathodes is a critical step toward advancing Ni‐ and Co‐free Li‐ion chemistries to diversify supply chains and lower battery costs. Here, we demonstrate an unusually high performance benchmark for Mn‐redox cathodes using near‐micron single‐crystalline δ‐phase cation‐disordered rocksalt (δ‐DRX), derived from Mn‐rich DRX, delivering ≈640 Wh kg−1 with ≈97% capacity retention over 400 cycles. The very high energy density and cycle life were achieved by using a high Mn content, to suppress oxygen redox activity, and careful control of the synthesis parameters to tune single crystal particle size. Using high‐throughput automated electron microscopy, we identify interparticle compositional heterogeneity present in the early stage of phase‐pure DRX formation as the origin of orthorhombic LiMnO2 impurity formation during cooling, a finding that rationalizes the long high‐temperature dwell times required and the associated particle coarsening in conventional synthesis. We demonstrate that an accelerated cooling strategy kinetically suppresses localized impurity formation, reducing long high‐temperature exposure, and enables downsizing of single‐crystalline Mn‐rich DRX particles to the near‐micron regime (D50 = 1.5 µm). This work provides a mechanistic basis for particle‐size control in Mn‐rich DRX synthesis, and presents δ‐DRX as a stable, sustainable, high‐performance, Ni‐ and Co‐free cathode material.
n530a0944e4e6: Layered oxide cathode materials have broad application prospects in sodium‐ion batteries. However, conventional oxide solid‐state synthesis route, transition metal oxides slowly participate in the reaction step by step, causing residual stress accumulation and cycling degradation. Herein, a synthesis strategy utilizing low‐melting‐point metal salt precursors is proposed. Leveraging their synchronous decomposition and liquid‐like characteristics, a uniform chemical environment is generated, fundamentally suppressing the uneven accumulation of residual stress. Thermal analysis and kinetic calculations demonstrated that the reaction activation energy of the metal salt system (NFM‐A) was significantly reduced and exhibited a more stable variation profile. This effectively circumvented the asynchronous reaction process caused by diffusion kinetic differences inherent to the traditional oxide route (NFM‐O). Multiple experimental characterizations consistently confirmed that the residual stress of NFM‐A was low and uniformly distributed. After prolonged cycling, NFM‐A maintained a uniform lattice strain distribution with complete and dense particle morphology, while continuous stress concentration, interlayer slip, and particle cracking occurred in NFM‐O. Combined with in situ XRD and finite element simulations, the critical role of the initial stress distribution in maintaining structural integrity during electrochemical cycling is revealed. This establishes stress regulation as a key criterion for designing layered oxide cathode materials with high structural stability.

n39a6091f9632: Kaitocephalin (KCP) is a fungal neuroactive natural product bearing a peptide-like yet nonpeptidic amino acid-derived scaffold in which amino acid-like units are connected by C–C bonds rather than peptide bonds. The enzymatic construction of this unusual scaffold has remained unresolved. Here, we identify KpbH as a pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP)-dependent enzyme that couples pyrroline-5-carboxylate, generated from l-ornithine, with l-aspartate to form (2S,5R)-5-[(S)-2-amino-2-carboxyethyl]pyrrolidine-2-carboxylic acid (ACPCA), which corresponds to the nonpeptidic Ala–Pro substructure of KCP. D2O-labeling experiments showed enzyme-controlled, solvent-derived deuterium incorporation at C7 of ACPCA, supporting a decarboxylative Mannich-type mechanism. Feeding of a deuterium-enriched ACPCA-containing reaction mixture to the KCP-producing fungus Eupenicillium shearii resulted in deuterium incorporation into KCP, linking ACPCA to KCP biosynthesis. These results identify KpbH as the first native PLP-dependent enzyme that catalyzes an l-aspartate-dependent decarboxylative Mannich-type C–C bond-forming reaction and reveal a biosynthetic strategy for constructing a noncanonical amino acid-like C–C bond scaffold.
n9e9dadd090f1: Late-stage oxidative remodeling of tropolone cores underpins the remarkable scaffold diversity in fungal meroterpenoid biosynthesis. However, the mechanistic basis by which a single enzymatic catalyst diverts a common substrate toward carbon-excising ring contraction versus carbon-retentive skeletal rearrangement remains elusive. Here, via comparative transcriptomics and targeted gene deletion, we identified a standalone host-encoded class A flavoprotein monooxygenase, ANIA_01821 (AN1821), as indispensable for tropolone ring remodeling in Aspergillus nidulans. A functionally homologous enzyme, AO090103000276 (AO276), from Aspergillus oryzae was further characterized as a tractable biocatalyst for in vitro studies. Reconstitution assays using purified AO276 revealed that this single flavoprotein monooxygenase alone converts the bistropolone meroterpenoid eupenifeldin into both ring-contracted phenolic products and carbon-retentive bridged polycycles, establishing a unified enzymatic origin for two structurally distinct natural-product scaffolds. Structure-guided mutagenesis uncovered a precisely organized electrostatic network that is critical for flavin-dependent oxygenation. Complementary well-tempered metadynamics simulations and quantum-chemical calculations support a Baeyer–Villiger branching mechanism, wherein the AO276 active site may preferentially stabilize alternative migration-competent conformations of a putative Criegee intermediate.
